units.title: Welcome to the Learning Garden
units.theme: Belonging, routines, names, classroom materials, and joyful learning
units.essentialQuestion: Who am I in this learning community?
units.mathFocus: Count, match, and sort classroom objects
units.inquiryFocus: Classroom community, safe routines, and responsibility

lessons.title: Wonder Launch
lessons.duration: 45–75 minute flexible learning block plus centers
lessons.objective: Introduce the unit question “Who am I in this learning community?” and use at least one example to notice or communicate an idea related to welcome to the learning garden.
teacherScript: Invite learners to share, point to, draw, sign, or select what they already notice about welcome to the learning garden.
Introduce the unit question: “Who am I in this learning community?” and model one answer using concrete materials or pictures.
Model the literacy focus: Names, print awareness, listening routines. Think aloud and repeat key words clearly.
Offer a short hands-on first attempt with the math focus: Count, match, and sort classroom objects. Let learners use objects, movement, drawings, words, or AAC.
Close by asking each learner to communicate one observation, question, or idea; note what needs modeling tomorrow.

lessons.title: Guided Skill Lab
lessons.duration: 45–75 minute flexible learning block plus centers
lessons.objective: Practise names, print awareness, listening routines and count, match, and sort classroom objects through guided, hands-on examples, then explain or show one strategy.
teacherScript: Quickly revisit Monday’s vocabulary and show one worked example connected to welcome to the learning garden.
Model the steps for names, print awareness, listening routines; say or show what to notice before asking learners to try.
Guide learners through count, match, and sort classroom objects using manipulatives, pictures, movement, or other accessible tools.
Give each learner a new example and gradually reduce prompts; ask “What helped you decide?”
Record one successful strategy and one misconception to revisit during Wednesday’s investigation.

lessons.title: Wonder Launch
lessons.duration: 45–75 minute flexible learning block plus centers
lessons.objective: Introduce the unit question “How do we learn by observing carefully?” and use at least one example to notice or communicate an idea related to the five senses.
teacherScript: Invite learners to share, point to, draw, sign, or select what they already notice about the five senses.

lessons.duration: 45–75 minute flexible learning block plus centers

items.label: Learning identity and help-seeking
items.prompt: Participates in a familiar learning routine and communicates a need for help, clarification, a break, or an access support through an appropriate mode.

items.label: Print and name awareness
items.prompt: Recognizes or uses meaningful print, name/label information, or another developmentally appropriate print concept in context.

items.label: Listening / receptive comprehension
items.prompt: Responds to a short story, explanation, signed/visual text, or accessible presentation with one relevant idea, answer, question, or selection.

items.label: Story sequence and retelling
items.prompt: Sequences and retells a three-part story with beginning, middle, and end while preserving important meaning rather than exact memorized wording.

items.label: Rhyme / patterned-language recognition
items.prompt: Identifies or generates an age-appropriate rhyme or equivalent patterned-language relationship through an appropriate spoken, signed, visual, tactile, or other accessible pathway.

items.label: Syllable / word-part segmentation
items.prompt: Segments and counts syllables or an appropriate language-pattern unit in familiar examples without confusing the count with written-letter count.

items.label: Beginning sound / letter relationship
items.prompt: Identifies a beginning phonological feature and demonstrates that written letters and spoken sounds are related but not perfectly one-to-one in an age-appropriate example.

items.label: Language access and variation
items.prompt: Uses an appropriate home-language, dialect, accent, signed-language, AAC, visual/tactile, or other access pathway without treating speech volume, hearing, eye contact, or one pronunciation as intelligence/mastery.

items.label: One-to-one counting
items.prompt: Counts a small set with one-to-one correspondence and states or represents the total accurately.

items.label: Cardinality and representation
items.prompt: Shows that the last count represents how many are in the set and represents the amount with objects, marks, numeral, tactile symbols, AAC, or another accessible form.

items.label: Quantity comparison
items.prompt: Counts and compares two sets using more, fewer, same, numerical totals, or an age-appropriate difference strategy.

items.label: Compose and decompose to 5
items.prompt: Builds or takes apart a quantity to 5 in more than one valid way and explains the parts/whole relationship.

items.label: Number-story meaning
items.prompt: Models a simple joining, separating, or part-part-whole situation and explains what the quantities represent.

items.label: Repeating pattern rule
items.prompt: Identifies, extends, repairs, or creates a repeating pattern and identifies the smallest repeating unit.

items.label: Shape properties
items.prompt: Describes a common two- or three-dimensional shape by relevant properties and recognizes that orientation, color, or size does not alone change its identity.

items.label: Spatial / map representation
items.prompt: Uses positional or directional language or a simple symbol/key to interpret or create a safe fictional route, map, or spatial model.

items.label: Fair length measurement
items.prompt: Measures or compares length/height from a common start using repeated equal-size units with no intentional gaps/overlaps.

items.label: Measurement communication and error detection
items.prompt: Reports a measurement as number plus unit and identifies or repairs an unfair measurement such as mixed units, shifted start, gaps, or overlaps.

items.label: Weight / capacity attribute reasoning
items.prompt: Distinguishes length/height from weight or capacity and uses evidence appropriate to the named attribute rather than visual size alone.

items.label: Rule-based classification
items.prompt: States a classification rule before sorting and sorts examples according to observable or known evidence.

items.label: Observation versus inference
items.prompt: Distinguishes what is directly observed from a guess, inference, prediction, or human-like story.

items.label: Prediction, evidence, and revision
items.prompt: Makes a simple prediction, compares it with evidence, and revises or qualifies the idea when evidence changes.

items.label: Weather / data reasoning
items.prompt: Uses a simple weather observation or graph/data display to make a supported present-tense comparison or claim without treating a short sample as a guaranteed forecast.

items.label: Plant structures and needs
items.prompt: Identifies common plant structures/functions or explains suitable access to water, light, air, space, and growing conditions without teaching soil as plant food.

items.label: Animal structures, needs, and humane care
items.prompt: Connects an animal structure/behavior or habitat feature to a need and knows wild animals are observed from a safe distance rather than fed, chased, captured, or handled.

items.label: Light, shadow, and Sun safety
items.prompt: Explains an age-appropriate light-source/object/shadow relationship and knows never to look directly at the Sun or use unsafe lasers, flames, heat, or lights aimed at eyes.

items.label: Earth rotation / day-night / seasonal care
items.prompt: Uses a simple Earth-rotation model for day/night and avoids claiming that winter or daylight patterns are identical everywhere.

items.label: Model purpose and limitation
items.prompt: Uses a map, habitat, plant, engineering, light, or other model for a stated purpose and names at least one thing the model leaves out or cannot prove.

items.label: Location privacy and navigation safety
items.prompt: Knows that home address, live location, school route, bus stop, or identifying location is not required and that a classroom route activity never authorizes independent travel.

items.label: Community work / goods / services
items.prompt: Distinguishes a good from a service or explains a community-care action without ranking jobs or stereotyping who performs work.

items.label: Needs, wants, and economic dignity
items.prompt: Explains a fictional need/want or resource choice in context and knows money, possessions, saving ability, housing, food access, or family finances do not determine human worth or responsibility.

items.label: Consent, helping, and voluntary sharing
items.prompt: Knows that kindness/helping never requires unsafe secrets, unwanted touch, forgiveness, money, gifts, food, comfort items, or surrendering personal possessions.

items.label: Safety and responsible tool use
items.prompt: Applies an appropriate trusted-adult, material, movement, plant/animal, weather, light, or classroom-tool safety boundary in a relevant scenario.

items.label: Engineering / fair-test revision
items.prompt: Tests or interprets a small safe model against a stated criterion under reasonably consistent conditions and uses evidence to revise or explain a design improvement.

items.label: Creative representation
items.prompt: Communicates an academic idea through drawing, building, movement, music/rhythm, dramatic representation, design, dictation, or another accessible creative form.

items.label: Self-regulation and persistence

items.label: Collaboration and respectful communication

items.label: Error analysis and repair

items.label: Listening comprehension

items.label: Story sequence

items.prompt: Tries a strategy and can explain or show what was changed, without speed being the goal.
